repairs.text: Strongest feature: Aron Ra identifies a testable implication: shared observation of one external spiritual environment should produce recognizable cross-report correspondence despite differences in memory, perspective, interpretation, and circumstance. Principal limitation: His interview claim remains evidentially underdeveloped because he specifies neither participant count, testimony, coding procedure, baseline variation, nor a comparative threshold showing that disagreement exceeds diversity among witnesses to external events. Live burden: He must document the inconsistencies, define the stable agreement external perception predicts, and compare observed patterns with internally generated experiences shaped by culture before the inference carries weight. Locked score: The locked score of 70 preserves the assessment’s balance: the proposed consistency test is intelligible, relevant, and responsive to separability reports, while anecdotal support, absolute wording, and subsidiary contact with Hernandez’s philosophical case restrict its force.

Strongest feature: Aron Ra offers a causal intervention: electronic brain stimulation produces sensed presences and out-of-body impressions resembling experiences people interpret as ghosts, demons, spiritual agents, or disembodied selves. Principal limitation: The account omits controls, participant selection, response frequency, effect size, independent replication, and quality, leaving unclear how the device caused these reactions or how representative they are of spontaneous experiences. Live burden: He must establish that stimulation produced the reported effects rather than suggestion or expectation, then justify how far those induced cases should lower confidence in unprompted reports without treating every report identically. Locked score: The locked score of 77 reflects a relevant physical alternative grounded in intervention rather than correlation, but sparse experimental detail and limited generalizability keep this evidence from independently resolving whether souls exist.
